I’d settled into my familiar perch by the window—a reclaimed oak table just wide enough for my fountain-pen journal and a well-thumbed copy of Estelle Maskame’s *Did I Mention I Love You?*. Beyond the glass, an autumn breeze coaxed golden leaves across the worn cobblestones, while inside the mingling aromas of freshly ground coffee and baked scones wrapped the room in quiet warmth. Between sips of Earl Grey, I inked a favourite line into the page, lingering over each curve of the letters, caught again by the way Maskame distils the shimmering ache of first love into words. From a far corner came soft laughter over cooling mugs, the sound folding neatly into the room’s gentle hum as I let the scene settle in me.
